papers.title_en: MAS-BIT: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-End BraIn-to-Text Decoding
papers.authors: Xinjie Zhang, Linyang He, Yizi Zhang, Yuesheng Ma, Nima Mesgarani
papers.evidence: 使用多智能体系统从皮层内记录进行端到端脑到文本解码
papers.tldr: 针对端到端脑到文本解码精度落后问题，提出多智能体系统MAS-BIT，通过神经、语音和仲裁三代理协同，利用token嵌入潜在通信融合神经表示与音素后验，在Brain-to-Text '24和'25基准上词错率分别达6.929%和3.606%，实现最先进端到端性能，无需集成或外部语言模型。
papers.abstract_en: Speech brain-computer interfaces aim to restore communication by translating neural activity into text, yet end-to-end decoders have historically trailed cascaded systems in accuracy. We introduce a Multi-Agent System for BraIn-to-Text (MAS-BIT), the first multi-agent framework for end-to-end brain-to-text decoding from intracortical recordings. MAS-BIT coordinates three specialized agents: a neural agent that interprets continuous neural representations, a phonetic agent that decodes soft phoneme posteriors, and an arbitration agent that integrates their complementary evidence with direct access to neural representations to generate the final transcription. The expert agents communicate with the arbiter through token-embedding-based latent communication, constructing continuous messages as probability-weighted combinations of token embeddings. These messages retain alternative token hypotheses and provide a differentiable interface through which sentence-level supervision jointly trains the neural encoders and specialized agents across participants. MAS-BIT achieves state-of-the-art end-to-end decoding performance on the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, with word error rates of 6.929% on '24 and 3.606% on the '25 public test set (3.892% on the private test set). These results surpass the published BIT cascade on the '25 public set and narrow the gap on '24, without ensembling independently trained models or using external language-model rescoring.

papers.title_en: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
papers.authors: Yuxiang Wei, Zundong Wu, Weiyu Sun, Qizhen Lan, Yanteng Zhang, Vince D. Calhoun
papers.evidence: 从神经观测中学习自然大脑动力学的世界模型
papers.tldr: 理解自然脑活动需超越刺激，捕捉个体动态脑状态。现有脑世界模型无法保持持续潜在状态，且标准指标无法判断是否跟踪个体状态。本文提出 BrainStateBench 基准，通过 State、Forecast、Updating 任务评估潜在状态，并设计 Spectator 线性潜在世界模型，用联合嵌入预测目标编码双时间尺度历史，实现状态跟踪与快速预测。Spectator 在 fMRI 预测和状态相关任务上全面超越仅刺激编码器和深度脑世界模型，预测速度提升 20 倍以上。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations. However, existing brain world models fail to maintain a persistent latent state over time, and standard metrics of neural prediction accuracy cannot tell whether a model tracks an individual's brain state or relies solely on the stimulus. To directly test state inference, prediction, and updating, we introduce BrainStateBench, which evaluates a model's latent state through a frozen linear probe on whole-cortex, movie-driven fMRI. Its State task tests whether a model captures trial-to-trial variability in an individual's responses to repeated stimuli, while Forecast and Updating evaluate future activity predictions without and with new observations, respectively. To track individual brain state across time, we propose Spectator, a linear latent world model trained with a joint-embedding predictive objective. Spectator encodes short- and long-horizon observation histories into a two-timescale latent state and predicts state transitions linearly from the current state and stimulus. Stimulus-only encoders reach 0.320 in fMRI prediction correlation without observing the brain (0% on State), while prior deep brain world models reach 0.239 yet score at most 0.4% on State. In contrast, Spectator achieves 0.349 correlation alongside 5.5% on State, 16.0% on Forecast, and 20.3% on Updating, outperforming all baselines while forecasting over 20x faster than deep forecasting models.

papers.title_en: SENSA: Visual-to-Brain Generation with Individualized Subject-State Transfer and Adaptation
papers.authors: Yihang Zou, Chunmei Qing, Ruixi Liang, Haichuan Wei, Junpeng Tan, Qifan Yang, Wanxiang Luo, Haodong Li, Xiangmin Xu, Yefeng Zheng
papers.evidence: 视觉到大脑编码预测神经反应，支持神经解码；主体自适应迁移
papers.tldr: 视觉到大脑编码面临共享/图像特异活动分离及跨被试分布偏移与表征异质性等挑战。SENSA框架通过独立响应先验捕获共享活动，用可分离传感器-时间基和共享响应细化器建模图像依赖响应，并结合被试自适应因子传输与源接地残差记忆，仅需少量配对数据即可个性化冻结生成器。在三个数据集上优于现有生成器，EEG与NSD仅400对图像校准下残差相关达0.1091和0.2995，验证了脑反应生成与跨被试适应的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Visual-to-brain encoding predicts neural responses to visual stimuli, supporting visual cognition research and neural decoding. However, challenges in disentangling shared from image-specific activity, together with inter-subject distribution shifts and representational heterogeneity, limit accurate encoding and cross-subject generalization with limited calibration data.   We introduce SENSA, a structured continuous neural response generation framework that separates shared activity from image-dependent responses and calibrates a compact subject state. An independent response prior captures shared activity, while complementary visual descriptors drive separable sensor-time bases and a shared Response Refiner. Subject-Adaptive Factor Transport adjusts the spatiotemporal expression of shared bases, while Source-Grounded Residual Memory predicts image-dependent corrections in source-response coordinates. Together, they personalize a frozen generator using limited paired support.   Experiments demonstrate that the generation backbone outperforms recent generators across three datasets, with image-identity perturbations confirming stimulus specificity. Using only 400 paired images, electroencephalography (EEG) and the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) calibration achieve residual Pearson correlations of 0.1091 and 0.2995, respectively, demonstrating effective brain-response generation and cross-subject adaptation.

papers.title_en: STAGE: Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling for Cross-Subject Brain-to-Image Retrieval
papers.authors: Yihang Zou, Ruixi Liang, Chunmei Qing, Junpeng Tan, Haichuan Wei, Wanxiang Luo, Gao Wu, Haodong Li, Xiangmin Xu, Yefeng Zheng
papers.evidence: 通过测试时自适应实现跨受试者脑信号解码以检索图像
papers.tldr: STAGE针对跨被试脑到图像检索中的个体差异和对齐困难，提出结构化测试时自适应框架，通过矩校准、耦合加权初始化和耦合引导自适应恢复对齐，并利用软耦合排序避免预测集中，仅用无标签目标批次且冻结编码器，在THINGS-EEG2上显著提升检索性能。
papers.abstract_en: Cross-subject brain-to-image retrieval aims to identify viewed images from unseen subjects' brain signals. However, inter-subject variability hinders alignment of brain-image representations, while independent query ranking tends to concentrate predictions on a few candidates, making accurate retrieval difficult without target labels. We propose STAGE (Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling), a structured test-time adaptation framework for recovering cross-subject alignment from uncertain brain-image correspondences. Moment calibration reduces statistical discrepancies between features, while coupling-weighted initialization establishes initial alignment. Coupling-guided adaptation further refines residual feature mismatches, and soft-coupling ranking coordinates candidate competition across queries to prevent overly concentrated matching assignments. Using only unlabeled target batches, STAGE maintains consistent matching from feature calibration to image retrieval while keeping both encoders frozen. Experiments on three public datasets validate STAGE's retrieval performance. On THINGS-EEG2, STAGE achieves 68.25% Top-1 and 90.47% Top-5, improving Top-1 by 18.52 percentage points over SCORE recovery and CSLS on identical frozen NICE features. Calibrated on 200 queries and a 200-image gallery covering their identities, STAGE retains 42.05% Top-1 when ranking 1,854 images with the transform frozen.

papers.title_en: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
papers.authors: Kieren Yu, Qian Zhang, Ziyang Liu, Chang Huang, Jintai Chen, Kaishun Wu
papers.evidence: 脑电图到图像解码基准标准化参与者访问方案
papers.tldr: 本文提出EVD-Bench基准，解决EEG到图像解码因参与者数据使用方式不同导致的比较混淆问题；在THINGS-EEG2上标准化设置，比较三种参与者访问制度，开展概念级零样本检索，并通过控制和变化因素系统评测，主张参与者访问制度应作为必要报告维度。
papers.abstract_en: EEG-to-image decoding recovers visual information from non-invasive brain recordings, providing a window into human perception. However, comparisons across systems are confounded by a variable that is rarely reported as such: which participants' data the system was allowed to use. The same Top-1 score on a 200-way gallery may come from a per-participant system, a pooled model over all participants, or a model that never saw the test participant---cases that differ by more than most architectural changes between the methods being compared. We present \bench, a benchmark on THINGS-EEG2 that standardizes the gallery and EEG input, matches training budgets across systems within each regime, and compares three participant-access regimes: within-subject, joint-subject, and strict leave-one-subject-out, with unlabeled target calibration reported separately. All three settings evaluate concept-level zero-shot retrieval: the 200 test concepts are disjoint from the 1,654 concepts used for EEG--image fitting and validation. We compare retrieval across access regimes and use zero-EEG and matched-wrong EEG controls to assess dependence on correct EEG--stimulus pairing. We vary trial averaging, gallery size and difficulty, and training data coverage, and compare target adaptation and visual feature targets. We also assess sensitivity to EEG window length and channel count, robustness to input perturbations, and confidence calibration. These results establish participant-access regime as a necessary reporting dimension alongside gallery, repetition, and visual target.

papers.title_en: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity
papers.authors: Weiheng Yao, Changhong Jing, Xuhang Chen, Chi-Man Pun, Michael Kwok-Po Ng, Shuqiang Wang
papers.evidence: 生成式框架对齐多模态脑活动并支持跨视觉和运动任务的解码
papers.tldr: 针对电生理与血流动力学数据配对采集难以扩展的问题，该研究提出一个生成框架，在统一表示空间中对齐多模态记录，并能从EEG生成fMRI BOLD与fNIRS血红蛋白反应。生成数据重现了区域动态、功能连接和任务结构，支持跨任务解码、独立记录解码和低样本增强，将皮层分析扩展到血流动力学数据稀疏的场景。
papers.abstract_en: Electrophysiological and haemodynamic recordings resolve brain activity at complementary temporal and spatial scales, yet paired acquisition remains difficult to scale. We propose a generative framework that aligns paired multimodal recordings in a unified representation space and generates modality-specific haemodynamic responses from EEG. In paired cohorts, the framework generated fMRI BOLD and fNIRS haemoglobin responses that reproduced regional dynamics, cortical maps, functional connectivity and task structure. Generated BOLD followed Real BOLD time courses and cortical patterns, while Generated haemoglobin responses tracked task-evoked HbO and HbR dynamics. The framework enabled decoding across visual, motor-imagery and mental-arithmetic tasks, independent-record decoding, external BOLD localization and low-sample augmentation. Paired feature-space calibration supported bidirectional retrieval. The proposed framework extends cortical analysis and brain decoding to EEG recordings when Real haemodynamic data are sparse.

papers.title_en: Beyond Full-Context Accuracy: Context-Marginalized Evaluation of Test-Time Structure-Aware Inference in EEG-to-Image Retrieval
papers.authors: Ke Xiao, Banghua Yang, Yingjie Li, Hang Zhang
papers.tldr: 测试时结构感知推理能提升跨被试EEG到图像检索，但预测依赖查询集组成；现有单一全上下文评估掩盖了上下文变化影响。本文提出上下文边缘化检索评估(CMRE)，通过采样上下文重复评估，区分结构可利用性与上下文鲁棒性。在THINGS-EEG2上，结构感知推理最高提升Top-1准确率20.40个百分点，但全上下文最优规则在70.8%条件下不再最优，平均损失2.70个百分点，且表示排名随上下文改变，表明CMRE提供了互补视角。
papers.abstract_en: Test-time structure-aware inference can improve cross-subject EEG-to-image retrieval by exploiting relations among unlabeled test queries, but it also makes predictions depend on query-set composition. Existing evaluations typically report accuracy under a single full-query context, leaving unclear whether gains and comparative conclusions hold as context changes. We introduce Context-Marginalized Retrieval Evaluation (CMRE), which repeatedly evaluates each target query in sampled contexts using the corresponding rows of a fixed query-gallery similarity matrix. CMRE distinguishes structural exploitability, quantified by gains over independent retrieval, from context robustness, measured by same-query Top-1 context consistency. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation on THINGS-EEG2 across six frozen representations and six structure-aware inference rules, structure-aware inference improves full-context Top-1 accuracy by up to 20.40 percentage points over independent retrieval. However, the rule selected under full-context evaluation is no longer optimal in 17 of 24 representation-context-size conditions (70.8%). Selecting the full-context winner incurs an average loss of 2.70 percentage points and a maximum loss of 8.29 percentage points under reduced contexts. Representation rankings are likewise inference- and context-dependent: the ordering under independent retrieval is not consistently preserved under structure-aware inference. Moreover, larger retrieval gains do not necessarily imply greater context robustness, showing that retrieval effectiveness and prediction stability provide complementary views of structure-aware inference. Full-context accuracy captures one operating point of context-dependent inference. CMRE complements it by characterizing how structural gains, context consistency, and comparisons of rules and representations change with query context.

papers.title_en: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
papers.authors: Josue Casco-Rodriguez, Nanda H. Krishna, Richard G. Baraniuk
papers.evidence: 噪声循环神经网络在重放中产生探索和时间压缩
papers.tldr: 本文重新审视噪声RNN中的重放为对类经历时间序列的Langevin采样，提出二阶Langevin框架：脉冲频率适应驱动空间探索，树突输入微分动量驱动时间压缩。在2D迷宫和合成大鼠位置细胞模拟中，适应与动量同时作用提高重放探索性与速度，首次在速率RNN中实现生物合理的时间压缩。
papers.abstract_en: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. We numerically verify our framework via simulations of noisy RNNs trained on 2D triangular and T-maze navigation activity, and others trained on place cell activity of synthetic rats. Crucially, we observe that simultaneous adaptation and momentum increases both replay exploration and speed, and provide one of the first accounts for biologically plausible temporal compression in rate-based RNN replay. Our findings encourage experiments into whether dendritic input differentiation, or other mechanisms, may support temporal compression in memory circuits like the hippocampus.

papers.title_en: History-bearing thalamocortical signals reconstruct and redirect later decisions in a circuit model
papers.evidence: 从丘脑皮层信号重建历史轨迹并影响决策
papers.tldr: 本研究探讨历史信息如何影响后续决策。基于小鼠后顶叶皮层和丘脑枕抑制数据，结合训练丘脑皮层回路模型，发现丘脑皮层输入可重建并重定向历史痕迹，其影响由循环动力学携带、当前感觉证据门控。精细空间组织和循环驱动对选择性塑造历史使用至关重要，且不破坏当前选择。
papers.abstract_en: Experience can guide an ambiguous choice or bias a choice despite strong current evidence. We asked how a thalamocortical circuit carries historical content forward and regulates its influence across successive decisions. In published data from adult male mice, suppressing posterior parietal cortex (PPC) or pulvinar (PUL) improved current judgments most when sensory history conflicted with the stimulus, reflecting reduced historical weighting. In trained thalamocortical circuit models, replaying recorded PUL input to PPC reconstructed a historical trace after equalizing complete recipient states across histories. Replaying the opposite history redirected the later choice, even after the circuit correctly judged an intervening strong stimulus. This historical message occupied a low-dimensional direction in thalamic output that remained broadly reachable under firing-rate bounds; redistributing the arriving current at matched energy showed that fine spatial organization, beyond total input strength, selectively shapes later history use without disrupting current choices. Strong sensory evidence suppressed historical output while preserving internal state differences, whereas ambiguity recruited neuronal rectification thresholds and readout alignment to express history. Small shifts in the cortical operating point modulated later historical influence, and partial attenuation of recurrent drive reduced it across all circuits while preserving current commitments; correspondingly, recurrent dynamics were essential for predicting post-stimulus trajectories in held-out histories. Together, these findings distinguish three operations in history-guided choice: returning thalamocortical input determines which past is reconstructed, recurrent dynamics carry its influence forward across intervening demands, and current sensory evidence gates how strongly it enters the decision.

papers.title_en: Spiking Neural Networks Incrementally Track Firing-Rate Networks
papers.evidence: 脉冲网络跟踪发放率网络的理论关联脉冲编码与速率编码
papers.tldr: 针对脉冲神经网络高效处理数据流的问题，本文提出SNN可增量跟踪对应firing-rate网络（ANN）的理论，并证明离散SNN输出持续跟踪由输入隐式确定的瞬时ANN输出。基于此开发LIF-Stream转换框架，通过重用先前激活状态和仅计算帧间更新来减少每帧时间步数，在三个流式推理基准上实现最佳效率-精度权衡。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding how spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently process data streams is key to (i) studying how biological brains conserve energy for lifelong predictions and (ii) enabling efficient continuous AI inference. In this work, we propose a theory on how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding firing-rate network, a continuous-valued neural network (ANN). We prove that the output of a discrete SNN continuously tracks the instantaneous ANN output implicitly determined by the SNN input. Based on this principle, we develop LIF-Stream, a conversion framework for efficient SNN inference over unbounded data streams. It enables the converted SNN to reuse its prior activation state and compute only the activation updates between frames, thereby reducing the average number of time steps needed per frame. Specifically, LIF-Stream controls the SNN to continuously track the reference ANN output, which gives a high-accuracy prediction for every frame. Evaluation on three large-scale streaming inference benchmarks with distinct modalities shows that LIF-Stream achieves the best efficiency-accuracy trade-off compared to high-accuracy SNN techniques.

papers.title_en: PhyMind: Physics-Informed Masked Autoencoding for EEG Foundation Models
papers.evidence: 物理信息掩码自编码用于EEG基础模型以改进解码
papers.tldr: 针对EEG基础模型预训练缺乏物理约束的问题，提出PhyMind，用生成式EEG前向模型替换掩码自编码器的解码器，通过68个皮层区域的阻尼振荡器与OU过程并投影到导联场进行物理信息重建。在相同设置下，其编码器token谱可解码性显著优于MAE和MANAS-2目标，接近大规模MANAS-2；下游冻结特征提升明显，但全微调略逊。
papers.abstract_en: EEG foundation models are pre-trained almost exclusively with masked reconstruction through a free-form decoder, sometimes with hand-crafted spectral targets added, as in MANAS-2. We study what happens when that decoder is replaced by a generative forward model of EEG. PhyMind keeps a standard masked transformer encoder, but its decoder must explain the masked signal through 68 cortical regions, each driven by damped stochastic oscillators and an aperiodic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, projected to the recording's own montage by a fixed boundary-element lead field evaluated per derivation. Training combines masked reconstruction with a Whittle spectral likelihood, an oscillator-dynamics residual, a minimum-norm source prior and a penalised neural residual. In a controlled comparison (same encoder, data, steps and seed), the physics decoder produces encoder tokens whose spectral content is far more linearly decodable than with a masked-autoencoder decoder or with the MANAS-2 objective: mean R^2 on a token-level spectral probe with amplitude-normalised targets is 0.67/0.77/0.77 on three datasets, against 0.24/0.50/0.50 (MAE) and 0.48/0.67/0.66 (MANAS-2 objective), approaching the released 92.8M-parameter MANAS-2 (0.71/0.81/0.80). Downstream gains in the controlled setting are small (four-task mean balanced accuracy 56.6 vs. 53.8 for MAE frozen, 63.8 vs. 62.7 fine-tuned). Region-level features from the physics decoder raise frozen four-class motor-imagery accuracy by 7-14 points, so a 7.2M-parameter model pre-trained on 3k hours of open EEG is comparable to the released MANAS-2 with frozen features (63.0 vs. 61.6). After full fine-tuning, MANAS-2 remains better (66.8 vs. 65.4 for our best model). The inferred sources do not reproduce the lateralisation that a classical inverse solution finds in motor imagery, so we do not claim anatomical interpretability. Code and weights are released.

papers.title_en: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Xiao Gu, Chao Zhang, Wen Wu, Shuaicong Hu, Qinfan Xiao, Jie Yang, Chen Chen, Wei Chen
papers.evidence: 组合预训练神经和心脏基础模型用于脑电睡眠表示学习
papers.tldr: SleepXA提出一种新框架，利用同步多导睡眠图组合独立预训练的EEG和ECG基础模型，通过睡眠引导对齐学习共享与模态特异表征。该框架在9230个PSG记录上预训练，并在27个下游任务中取得22项前两名，表明同步多模态生理信号可作为组合现有生理基础模型的自然接口，产生可扩展至临床和日间场景的可复用表征。
papers.abstract_en: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.
